beats.narration_text: Subtracting the largest score changes the weights, not the distribution. It stops overflow at the top; it does nothing about underflow at the bottom. Here is the evidence, from real code.

props.text:
Why subtract the max first?
It changes the distribution.
It stops overflow.

beats.narration_text: The course's reference implementation does not exponentiate your scores. It finds the largest one and subtracts it from all of them first. Scores one, two, three become minus two, minus one, zero. That is the whole of this video: what did that subtraction change?

props.title: The Move Nobody Explains
props.footnote: Recorded output · evidence_output.json · case A · Windows 11 · Python 3.14.2

beats.narration_text: Each shifted score goes through the exponential. The largest score is now exactly zero, so its weight is exactly one. Every other weight is smaller than one. Add them: one point five oh three two. Divide each weight by that total, and those are the probabilities.

props.title: Watch the Numbers Move
props.footnote: Recorded output · evidence_output.json · case A · Windows 11 · Python 3.14.2

beats.narration_text: Here is the reason it is safe. Exponentiating a difference splits into a product: e to the z-i over T, times e to the minus m over T. That second factor is the same in every numerator — and it is in every term of the denominator too. It cancels. The intermediate weights changed. The ratio between any two of them did not, and the ratio is the whole distribution.

show.event: row 2: common factor exp(-m/T) top and bottom, terracotta
row 3: unshifted form (the factor is gone)

props.title: Why It Is Allowed
props.conditions: m = maxⱼ zⱼ · T > 0 · identity from Chapter 1, Part 2

beats.narration_text: That is the algebra. Here is the run. The evidence script computed the same distribution twice for scores one, two, three — once the shifted way, once straight from the original scores. Largest absolute difference between them: one point one one times ten to the minus sixteen. That is floating-point noise, not a different distribution.

show.event: recorded case A output: reference_shifted, direct_unshifted, max_abs_difference

beats.narration_text: Now the case the shift is actually for. Two equal scores of one thousand. Straight exponentiation does not return a wrong answer — it does not return at all. OverflowError, math range error. Subtract the maximum and the same input becomes zero, zero; weights one, one; total two; one half and one half. The thousand was in both entries. It never carried any information about which outcome is preferred, and it never needed to reach the exponential.

show.event: right lane builds to [0.5, 0.5] on each spoken value

props.title: Where the Direct Route Stops Existing
props.footnote: Recorded output · evidence_output.json · case B · Windows 11 · Python 3.14.2

beats.act: F · what this does not establish
beats.narration_text: One boundary, and the chapter names it: keep the claim narrower than "numerically stable." Take scores zero and minus one thousand. The maximum is already zero, so subtracting it changes nothing, and e to the minus one thousand underflows to exactly zero point zero. The function returns one and zero. The real second probability is about five point oh eight times ten to the minus four hundred thirty-five — vanishingly small, but not zero. Subtracting the maximum removes overflow at the top. It does nothing about underflow at the bottom, and it does not tell you it happened.

props.title: What This Does Not Establish
props.footnote: Chapter 1: “Keep the tested claim narrower than the slogan ‘numerically stable.’” · evidence_output.json · case C · Windows 11 · Python 3.14.2

cue_phrases.float: and e to the minus one thousand

beats.narration_text: The verdict. Subtracting the maximum changes the intermediate weights, not the distribution, because e to the minus m over T cancels. It turns an overflow on one thousand, one thousand into one half, one half. It is not numerical stability: zero, minus one thousand still underflows to exactly zero.

show.event: verdict: the claim, then one line per evidence case

artifactLines: Changes the weights, not the distribution: the factor exp(−m/T) cancels.
Case A: the two routes differ by at most 1.1102230246251565e-16.

Case C: [0, -1000] still returns [1.0, 0.0] — not numerical stability.
